name: awandesign-mcp

tools.name: open_editor
tools.description: Open the Awan Design editor in the user's default browser and ask them to connect it to this MCP server. The user must click "Allow" in the "Connect AI" dialog that appears in the editor (a security step that cannot be skipped). Call this first when editor_status says the editor is not connected. Then call editor_status to confirm the connection.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the user to allow the connection (default 90, 0 = do not wait).

tools.name: editor_status
tools.description: Check whether the Awan Design editor is connected, and summarize the current design (size, number of objects).

tools.name: new_design
tools.description: Create a new blank design and open it in the editor (replaces the current canvas; the previous design stays saved in the user's projects). Do this ONLY when the user asks for a fresh/blank canvas; to add content to what is already there, use the template or add_* tools instead. The canvas can be infinite (auto-sizing): set infinite=true and omit width/height unless the user wants a fixed size. Common sizes: Instagram post 1080x1080, Instagram story 1080x1920, Facebook post 1200x630, YouTube thumbnail 1280x720, A4 portrait 2480x3508.

infinite.description: Infinite canvas: the canvas grows automatically to fit its content, so no size is needed

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: List every object on the canvas (id, type, position, size, text, colors) so you can reference them in update_object / delete_object.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the designs saved in the user's browser (id, name, last updated).

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Load a saved design by id (from list_projects) into the editor.

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Force-save the current design to the browser storage. (The editor also auto-saves.)

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change in the editor.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change in the editor.

tools.name: add_text
tools.description: Add a text box. Coordinates are canvas pixels with the origin at the top-left. Omit x/y to center it.

width.description: Wrap width in px; omit for a single auto-width line

fontFamily.description: Any font bundled in Awan Design, e.g. Poppins, Inter, Roboto, Montserrat, Playfair Display (default Poppins)

tools.name: add_shape
tools.description: Add a shape. shape: rect, circle (ellipse if width != height), triangle, line, or any built-in id such as diamond, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, star5, star4, arrowRight, arrowLeft, arrowUp, arrowDown, heart, plus, cloud, shield, message, moon, or a flowchart symbol (fc_process, fc_decision, fc_database, fc_startend, ...; see list_shapes) which becomes a diagram node that add_connector can link. Omit x/y to center it.

text.description: Optional label centered on the shape

tools.name: create_component
tools.description: Create a cohesive, mathematically centered UI component (buttons, 3D pill toggles, feature cards, checklist items, badges) with background shape, optional 3D gloss bevel, Lucide concept icon or brand logo, and typography in a single grouped object. Use this instead of manually calculating coordinates or drawing raw SVG paths for UI elements.

shape.description: Component container shape (default "rect", "pill" has rounded end-caps)

bevel.description: Add subtle 3D gloss highlight at the top for pressable button appearance (default false)

icon_size.description: Icon size in px (default ~45% of height)

gap.description: Gap between icon and text in px (default 12)

name.description: Layer name for the component group

tools.name: add_image
tools.description: Add an image. source can be a local file path, an http(s) URL, or a data URL - the MCP server reads it and sends it to the editor, so CORS is not an issue. Alternatively pass gallery_id (from list_gallery) to use an image already in the user's gallery. Omit width/height to fit the image within 80% of the canvas. Omit x/y to center.

tools.name: add_svg
tools.description: Import your own SVG as an editable vector group. source can be raw SVG markup, a local file path, or an http(s) URL. For brand/tech logos prefer search_icons + add_icon (built-in library).

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Search Awan Design built-in SVG library of brand and technology logos (thousands: Vercel, Nginx, Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, Vue, React, AWS, Google Cloud, GitHub, Slack, ...). Returns slugs usable with add_icon and with the "icon" field of create_diagram nodes. Search by product name, e.g. "postgres", "kafka", "cloudflare".

tools.name: add_icon
tools.description: Place a brand/tech logo from the built-in library (see search_icons) on the canvas as an editable vector. Omit x/y to center it.

tools.name: list_gallery
tools.description: List images stored in the user's Awan Design gallery (assets they uploaded earlier). Use add_image with gallery_id to place one.

tools.name: update_object
tools.description: Change properties of an object by id (see get_design / get_object). Only pass what you want to change. Parts inside a group (e.g. one path of an imported SVG, ids shown by get_object) accept only fill, stroke, strokeWidth, opacity, visible and name. For diagram nodes and connectors, "label" edits the attached label; moving a node automatically re-routes its connectors.

label.description: Label text for diagram nodes / connectors

line_style.description: Line style of a connector, or the border of a shape/path

source_side.description: Connection point on source node (for connectors)

target_side.description: Connection point on target node (for connectors)

offset_x.description: Middle vertical segment offset for connectors in px

offset_y.description: Middle horizontal segment offset for connectors in px

label_dx.description: Horizontal offset for connector label in px

label_dy.description: Vertical offset for connector label in px

tools.name: delete_object
tools.description: Delete an object by id. Deleting a diagram node also deletes its label and attached connectors.

tools.name: create_diagram
tools.description: Create a custom graph (general architecture / org chart / network topology) from nodes and edges. NOT for UML Use Case diagrams (use create_usecase_diagram) or SOP flowcharts (use create_flowchart). Positions are computed by an automatic layered layout, connectors are real editor connectors (they follow nodes when the user drags them), and every node gets an editable label. Give each node a short unique id and readable text; use kind to pick the symbol: service, process, database, queue, cache, user, external, decision, terminal, cloud. Use color names (blue, green, orange, purple, red, yellow, teal, pink, gray) or hex to group components visually (e.g. all databases green). To show a product logo inside a node, set its "icon" to a slug found with search_icons (built-in library of brand/tech logos). After creating, call get_preview to check the result and fix issues with update_object.

title.description: Optional heading shown above the diagram

text.description: Label; use \n for a line break

icon.description: Optional logo slug from search_icons (e.g. "nginx", "postgresql"); shown at the left inside the node

style.description: Line style (default solid); the arrowhead always stays solid

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

new_design.description: Deprecated alias of replace. Default behavior: the diagram is added next to existing content (or at x, y if given); nothing is deleted.

name.description: Design name when new_design is true

tools.name: create_flowchart
tools.description: USE WHEN creating flowcharts, business processes, algorithms, or SOPs. Highly token-efficient: supply a list of steps, and the server automatically applies ISO 5807 flowchart symbols (start/end terminal, decision diamond, process rectangle, database cylinder), auto-wraps long text cleanly, applies harmonious colors, and connects branches (yes/no or auto-chaining). Call get_preview afterwards.

id.description: Unique ID for this step, e.g. "start", "check_login", "dashboard"

text.description: Step description; automatically wrapped if long

color.description: Color: blue, green, orange, purple, red, yellow, teal, pink, gray

icon.description: Optional brand/tech icon slug from search_icons

next.description: Target step ID (for linear sequence; if omitted, automatically connects to the next step in array)

next_label.description: Optional text on arrow to next step

yes.description: Target step ID when decision is Yes/True (default label "Ya")

yes_label.description: Custom label for yes arrow, e.g. "Valid", "Approved"

no.description: Target step ID when decision is No/False (default label "Tidak")

no_label.description: Custom label for no arrow, e.g. "Invalid", "Rejected"

branches.description: Additional branching routes from this step

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

tools.name: create_usecase_diagram
tools.description: USE WHEN the user asks for a UML Use Case Diagram. NOT for flowcharts / step-by-step logic (use create_flowchart) or server architecture (use create_system_design). Creates a clean, industry-standard Use Case diagram in one call: primary actors on the left, secondary/system actors on the right, system boundary box with title, neatly spaced horizontal usecase ovals inside the boundary, and straight association lines (no arrowheads) plus dashed <<include>> / <<extend>> connectors. Layout and spacing are calculated mathematically without collision. Read awandesign://guides/usecase for details. Afterwards call get_preview.

title.description: Main title above the diagram, e.g. "Use Case Diagram: Sistem Kasir"

system_name.description: System name displayed inside the System Boundary, e.g. "Sistem Kasir Restoran"

side.description: left = primary actor (default), right = secondary / system actor

actors.description: Actors (stickman figures) placed on the left or right of boundary

label.description: Use case text, e.g. "Login ke Akun"

usecases.description: Use case ovals inside the boundary

from.description: Source actor or use case ID

to.description: Target use case or actor ID

relations.description: Relationships between actors and use cases (association, include, extend, generalization)

target.description: Use case ID this note attaches to

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

tools.name: get_preview
tools.description: Render the design as an image so you can visually check your work (text clipped? arrows overlapping? layout balanced?). After a template tool placed a design next to existing content, pass its "area" as region to see only the new design.

object_id.description: Render only this object instead of the whole design

region.description: Render only this rectangle (canvas px), e.g. the "area" returned by a template tool, to check a new design placed next to an old one

tools.name: export_design
tools.description: Export the design as PNG, JPG, or SVG and save it in the export folder the user configured (AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_DIR in .mcp.json, default ~/Downloads). ASK THE USER FIRST where/whether to save, then pass user_approved: true. Without approval nothing is written. Returns the saved file path.

object_id.description: Export only this object (png/jpg) instead of the whole design

output_path.description: File name or path inside the export folder (AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_DIR). Default: <design-name>.<ext>

user_approved.description: Set true ONLY after the user agreed to save the file at the location shown. Not needed when the user set AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_AUTO_APPROVE=true.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Return the objects the user currently has selected in the editor. Use it for requests like "fix the thing I selected" or "make this bigger".

tools.name: select_object
tools.description: Select one or more objects by id so the user can see them highlighted. Pass an empty list to clear the selection.

tools.name: get_object
tools.description: Full details of one object: size, scale, flips, text style, image size, edge cleanup, device info, and children of a group (e.g. each path of an imported SVG, which update_object can recolor).

tools.name: duplicate_object
tools.description: Duplicate an object (diagram nodes keep their label and icon). Not for connectors/labels.

tools.name: reorder_object
tools.description: Move an object forward/backward one step, or to the front/back, within its layer group.

tools.name: align_objects
tools.description: Align objects to the canvas (default) or to each other, and/or distribute them evenly (needs 3+ objects). Diagram nodes keep their labels and connectors in sync. Prefer this over computing coordinates by hand.

to.description: Reference: the canvas (default) or the bounding box of the given objects

tools.name: group_objects
tools.description: Group 2+ objects into one. Not for diagram nodes/connectors/labels.

tools.name: ungroup_object
tools.description: Break a group into its individual objects.

tools.name: add_path
tools.description: Draw a custom vector shape from SVG path data (the "d" attribute), e.g. "M0 0 L100 0 L50 80 Z". Use for custom shapes, curves, and freehand-like lines.

tools.name: list_shapes
tools.description: List every shape id usable with add_shape, including the flowchart symbols (fc_*).

tools.name: list_fonts
tools.description: Search the fonts bundled with Awan Design (hundreds of Google fonts). Use the exact name with add_text / update_object fontFamily.

tools.name: add_connector
tools.description: Add an arrow connector between two diagram nodes (nodes from create_diagram, fc_* / uc_* symbols, or objects made nodes with set_diagram_node). Sides are chosen automatically unless given. The connector follows the nodes when they move or rotate.

source_side.description: Source connection point (e.g. top, bottom, left, right, top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right)

target_side.description: Target connection point (e.g. top, bottom, left, right, top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right)

line_style.description: Default solid. Users can also change it in the editor (Properties panel > Line style).

arrow_type.description: Arrowhead style: 'none' (solid line, no arrow, for UML association), 'default' (open arrow for include/extend/directed), 'triangle' (closed triangle for UML generalization)

end_arrow.description: false to omit arrowheads (same as arrow_type: 'none')

source_shift.description: Shift the start point along its side in px, to run several parallel connectors between the same two nodes

target_shift.description: Shift the end point along its side in px

route_shape.description: Path shape: elbow (default, right angles), straight, or curve. Users can change it in the Properties panel.

font.description: Font family of the label; use the same family as the rest of the design

offset_x.description: Move the middle vertical segment of the route sideways in px (route around other nodes)

offset_y.description: Move the middle horizontal segment of the route up/down in px

tools.name: set_diagram_node
tools.description: enabled=true makes any shape connectable with add_connector (same as "Convert to diagram" in the editor). enabled=false removes its connectors, label and icon.

tools.name: crop_image
tools.description: Crop an image object to a rectangle. x/y/width/height are in pixels of the image as it is currently displayed (0,0 = its top-left corner; see its size via get_object). as_new=true keeps the original and adds the crop as a new layer.

tools.name: auto_slice
tools.description: Split an image containing several separate objects (transparent or solid background) into one layer per object, kept at the same canvas positions.

tools.name: remove_background
tools.description: Remove the background of an image using the on-device AI model. Slow on first use (model download, up to a few minutes); do not call in parallel.

tools.name: edge_cleanup
tools.description: Erode leftover fringe pixels (e.g. after remove_background) and optionally blur the alpha edge. distance and blur of 0 remove the filter.

tools.name: enhance_image
tools.description: Upscale and sharpen an image 2x using the on-device AI model. Slow for large images.

tools.name: power_clip
tools.description: Mask an image with a shape: the shape becomes the visible window onto the image. Release later with release_power_clip.

fit.description: cover (default): scale and center the image so it fills the whole shape. none: keep the image where it is (only the part overlapping the shape shows).

tools.name: release_power_clip
tools.description: Undo power_clip: restore the original image and shape as separate objects.

tools.name: save_to_gallery
tools.description: Store an image in the user's gallery for reuse. Provide source (file path / URL / data URL) or object_id (renders that object as a transparent PNG).

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List device mockup types for add_device (phones, tablet, laptop, desktop) and the Polaroid frame.

tools.name: add_device
tools.description: Add a device frame (see list_devices) and optionally fill its screen with a screenshot (file path / URL / data URL). For type "polaroid", screenshot is the photo and caption is the handwritten text below it.

type.description: iphone, pixel, tablet, laptop, desktop or polaroid

tools.name: list_layers
tools.description: List the layer groups (parent layers) and the objects in each. New objects go into the active layer group.

tools.name: add_layer_group
tools.description: Create a new layer group and make it active, so objects added afterwards go into it.

tools.name: set_layer_group
tools.description: Rename a layer group, show/hide it, or make it the active one.

tools.name: move_to_layer_group
tools.description: Move an object (with its label/icon) into a different layer group.

tools.name: add_guide
tools.description: Add a horizontal or vertical guide line at a canvas position (visible in the editor, not exported).

tools.name: remove_guide
tools.description: Remove a guide by id (ids are listed in get_design).

tools.name: set_zoom
tools.description: Change the editor view: mode "fit" (fit to screen), "reset" (100%), or a numeric level such as 0.5. Does not affect exports.

tools.name: set_canvas
tools.description: Resize the current design, change its background color, or toggle the infinite canvas. Existing objects are not moved.

tools.name: rename_project
tools.description: Rename the open design (omit id) or a saved project.

tools.name: duplicate_project
tools.description: Save a copy of the open design (omit id) or of a saved project. The copy is not opened.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Permanently delete a saved project. ALWAYS ask the user for confirmation first, then pass confirm: true. The open design cannot be deleted.

confirm.description: Must be true; only after the user confirmed

tools.name: export_project_file
tools.description: Write the open design to a .awandesign file in the export folder the user configured (AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_DIR in .mcp.json, default ~/Downloads). ASK THE USER FIRST, then pass user_approved: true.

output_path.description: File name or path inside the export folder

user_approved.description: Set true ONLY after the user agreed to save the file at the location shown. Not needed when the user set AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_AUTO_APPROVE=true.

tools.name: import_project_file
tools.description: Load a .awandesign (or .json) project file from this computer into the editor as a new project.

tools.name: create_hld_poster
tools.description: USE WHEN the user describes an ORDERED INTEGRATION FLOW between systems (steps, endpoints, tokens, request/response). NOT for explaining an app or concept (use create_hld_explainer) and not for free-form graphs (use create_diagram). If the user did not choose a template, call suggest_template and let THEM choose before calling this; the tool refuses to run without the template_token that suggest_template issues. Create a polished High Level Diagram poster in one call: one colored system card per system (any number: 2 systems = 2 cards, 10 systems = 10 cards, wrapped into rows) (with logos/illustrations and detail panels), numbered arrows between neighbouring systems (solid or dashed, with labels and "POST /path" notes), and a "Flow Description" panel with one card per step. Use it for integration / API / data-pipeline / notification flows described in words; the user does NOT need to provide a reference image. Layout, sizes, colors and fonts are computed automatically. For free-form graphs with many branches or loops use create_diagram instead. Read the resource awandesign://guides/hld-poster (or prompt hld_poster) for how to turn a description into this spec. Afterwards call get_preview and fix any clipped text with update_object.

id.description: Id used by flows (default col1, col2, ...)

color.description: blue = data source, purple = orchestrator, yellow = gateway, green = destination

icon_label.description: Large text under the logo, e.g. "n8n"

illustration.description: Built-in drawing when no logo fits

outline_icon.description: Concept icon (Lucide name from search_outline_icons, e.g. "Bot", "Layers") for cards without a brand logo. Every card always gets a visual: if none of icon / illustration / outline_icon is set, an icon is chosen automatically from the title.

lines.description: Lines of text; bullets are added automatically for style "list"

columns.description: ONE CARD PER SYSTEM: 2 systems -> 2 cards, 10 systems -> 10 cards (wrapped into rows automatically, zig-zag so consecutive systems stay adjacent). List them in flow order, source first.

to.description: Adjacent column id (to the left of "from" = arrow points left)

step.description: Step number shown as a badge; matches the position in steps[]

style.description: solid = main data flow; dashed = auth/token/response; dotted / dashdot also available (the arrowhead stays solid)

color.description: navy (default for solid), blue (default for dashed), green, teal, orange, red, gray, pink, or hex

flows.description: Arrows between adjacent systems: consecutive systems are always adjacent; also left/right neighbours in a row and top/bottom neighbours between rows

steps.description: One per numbered flow, in order; shown in the Flow Description panel (wrapped into rows when many)

columns_per_row.description: Cards per row; default automatic (all in one row up to 5, then balanced rows)

template_token.description: REQUIRED. Token from suggest_template, issued only after the user chose this template (or delegated the choice). One token = one design. Never invent one.

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

mode.description: diagram (default): cards are real diagram nodes and arrows are real editor connectors that stay attached when the user moves a card, and whose line style the user can change in the Properties panel. poster: static drawing only.

tools.name: create_hld_explainer
tools.description: USE WHEN the user asks to EXPLAIN or give an OVERVIEW of an application/project/concept ("HLD of this project", "what is HLD", onboarding, documentation, infographic). NOT for ordered integration flows with endpoints (use create_hld_poster) and not for free-form graphs (use create_diagram). If the user did not choose a template, call suggest_template and let THEM choose before calling this; the tool refuses to run without the template_token that suggest_template issues. Create a one-page explainer infographic in one call: a definition banner, a left panel of key focus areas and a right panel of key questions (both with outline icons), an example architecture diagram in the middle (grid-placed nodes with icons and REAL editor connectors: solid, dashed, bidirectional), and a "Why it matters" footer with benefit tiles. Use it to EXPLAIN a system or concept (onboarding, documentation, "what is HLD") from a plain description; no reference image needed. For numbered integration flows use create_hld_poster; for free-form graphs use create_diagram. Read the resource awandesign://guides/hld-explainer (also contains general HLD knowledge) or prompt hld_explainer, and find icon names with search_outline_icons. Afterwards call get_preview.

text.description: 1-2 sentence definition; "\n" for a line break

icon.description: Lucide icon name from search_outline_icons, e.g. "Puzzle", "Database", "ShieldCheck"

icons.description: Several icons stacked in a "tall" node (e.g. Monitor, Smartphone, Laptop for clients)

caption.description: Small text at the bottom of a "tall" node, e.g. "Web / Mobile / TV"

color.description: Groups component types: purple = gateway/engine, blue = auth/analytics, orange = business service/edge, green = content/core

style.description: solid = main flow; dashed = supporting flow (auth, control)

template_token.description: REQUIRED. Token from suggest_template, issued only after the user chose this template (or delegated the choice). One token = one design. Never invent one.

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

tools.name: search_outline_icons
tools.description: Find Lucide outline icon names for create_hld_explainer (e.g. "database", "shield", "users", "cloud", "chart"). Works without the editor. For brand/tech logos use search_icons instead.

tools.name: suggest_template
tools.description: Call this FIRST whenever the user asks for a diagram/HLD without naming a template. If the user did not choose a template it returns decision "ask" with numbered options: show those options to the user (use a choice prompt tool if you have one, otherwise a plain list), then STOP and WAIT for their reply; do not create anything and do not choose for them. Only when the user explicitly delegates ("terserah", "you choose", "up to you") call it again with delegated=true: it then returns decision "use" with the template to use. If the request already names a template/style it returns "use" directly. Without a request it returns the whole catalog. Works without the editor. After creating, tell the user which template was used and offer the other.

request.description: The user's request, in their own words

delegated.description: true ONLY when the user explicitly left the choice to you (e.g. "terserah")

chosen.description: The template id the USER picked from the numbered options (or re-issue for the same template to fix the design you just created). Never set it on your own.

tools.name: create_system_design
tools.description: USE WHEN the user wants a classic system-design / scalable-architecture diagram: users, DNS, CDN, load balancer, web servers, cache, database master/replica, message queue, shards, multiple data centers. NOT for numbered integration flows (use create_hld_poster), a one-page explainer (use create_hld_explainer) or flowcharts/org charts (use create_diagram). If the user did not choose a template, call suggest_template and let THEM choose before calling this; the tool refuses to run without the template_token that suggest_template issues. Two ways: (1) pass "pattern" for a ready-made blueprint (single-server, web-db-split, load-balancer, db-replication, cache-tier, cdn, multi-dc, message-queue, sharding, full-stack), optionally with title/subtitle overrides; (2) pass your own nodes/edges/zones. Nodes have an icon and optional xN replica stack; zones are labeled boxes grouping nodes (a tier or a data center); arrows are REAL editor connectors (solid/dashed/dotted, bidirectional) so the user can drag and restyle them. Layout is automatic. Nodes/edges/zones passed together with a pattern are ADDED to it. Read awandesign://guides/system-design. Afterwards call get_preview.

kind.description: Picks a default icon and color: user, client, mobile, dns, cdn, loadbalancer, gateway, web, app, service, cache, database, replica, queue, worker, storage, search, auth, monitor, external, shard

sublabel.description: Small text under the name, e.g. "Redis", "Write", "IP publik"

icon.description: Lucide icon name (search_outline_icons) overriding the kind default

zone.description: id of the zone (container box) this node sits in

replicas.description: Show as a stack of N identical instances with an xN badge

label.description: Short text on the arrow, e.g. "HTTP", "baca", "tulis", "replikasi"

template_token.description: REQUIRED. Token from suggest_template, issued only after the user chose this template (or delegated the choice). One token = one design. Never invent one.

replace.description: Default false: an existing design is NEVER deleted; the new design is placed in empty space to its right. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas and recreate it (the old design stays saved in the projects list). The canvas is infinite, so never specify a canvas size.

font.description: Font family for the WHOLE design (one family only; a name from list_fonts, e.g. "Inter", "Poppins", "Roboto"). Default "Inter". Never mix families in one design.

instructions:
Awan Design is a browser-based graphic design editor. These tools create designs, posters and diagrams live in the user's open editor tab.
Start with editor_status; if not connected, call open_editor and ask the user to click "Allow" in the Connect AI dialog.
ASSETS: the editor ships a built-in library of thousands of brand/tech SVG logos (Vercel, Nginx, Docker, PostgreSQL, Vue, AWS, GitHub, ...). Use search_icons to find a logo by name, then add_icon to place it, or set "icon" on a create_diagram node so the logo appears inside the node. Prefer these built-in logos over drawing your own SVG. The user's image gallery is available through list_gallery + add_image(gallery_id).
DIAGRAMS: use create_flowchart for business logic / processes / SOPs (compact steps schema, auto-chaining, ISO symbols); use create_usecase_diagram for UML Use Case Diagrams (actors, system boundary, usecase ovals, associations, include/extend); use create_diagram for custom graphs. Always call get_preview afterwards to check the result, then fix with update_object.
Fonts: any bundled Google font works (search with list_fonts), e.g. Poppins, Inter, Roboto, Montserrat, Playfair Display.
EDITING: get_selection returns what the user has selected ("fix this"); get_object gives details (including paths inside an imported SVG, recolorable via update_object). Use align_objects, reorder_object, duplicate_object, group_objects instead of calculating coordinates by hand; add_path draws custom vectors from SVG path data; add_connector links diagram nodes (fc_* flowchart shapes and create_diagram nodes).
IMAGES: crop_image, remove_background and enhance_image (on-device AI, slow: call one at a time), edge_cleanup, auto_slice (sprite sheets), power_clip (fill a shape with an image). add_device places phone/laptop/desktop mockups and Polaroids with a screenshot.
EXISTING CONTENT AND CANVAS SIZE: never delete or overwrite what is already on the canvas. Template tools (create_hld_poster, create_hld_explainer, create_system_design, create_diagram) put the new design in empty space to the right of the existing content; the "area" in the tool result tells you where (pass it as region to get_preview). Only when the user explicitly asks to delete/clear/replace the previous canvas, call the tool with replace=true. The editor uses an infinite canvas that sizes itself to the content, so never choose or set a canvas size for templates. CHOOSING A TEMPLATE (do not guess from the word "HLD" alone): 1. Bila user SUDAH menyebut template atau gayanya (mis. "poster", "explainer", "infografis", "flowchart"), pakai template itu tanpa bertanya. 2. Bila user TIDAK menyebut template: JANGAN memilih sendiri dan jangan membuat desain dulu. Panggil suggest_template dengan kalimat user; hasilnya "ask" berisi daftar opsi bernomor. Tampilkan opsi itu ke user (pakai alat tanya pilihan bila ada, selain itu daftar teks) dan TUNGGU balasan user. Rekomendasi boleh disebut, tetapi bukan keputusan. 3. Setelah user memilih opsi, panggil suggest_template dengan chosen=<id template>; hasilnya memuat template_token. Tool create_hld_poster / create_hld_explainer / create_system_design menolak berjalan tanpa token itu (satu token = satu desain). 4. HANYA bila user mendelegasikan ("terserah", "bebas", "kamu pilih saja", "up to you"): panggil suggest_template lagi dengan delegated=true lalu pakai rekomendasinya. 5. Setelah membuat, sebutkan template yang dipakai dan tawarkan template lain yang relevan. Mengganti template murah: cukup panggil tool lain. Templates: create_hld_poster (numbered system-flow poster), create_hld_explainer (one-page explainer infographic), create_system_design (classic system-design architecture: load balancer, cache, replicas, zones; has ready-made patterns), create_diagram (free-form graph). The user only needs to describe the subject in words, never to attach a reference image. Details: resource awandesign://guides/templates, awandesign://guides/hld-poster, awandesign://guides/hld-explainer, awandesign://guides/flowchart, awandesign://guides/usecase, awandesign://guides/activity. search_outline_icons finds concept icons (Database, ShieldCheck, Users...) for the explainer.
UI COMPONENTS & BUTTONS: To create buttons, 3D pill toggles, feature cards, checklist items, or badges, use create_component. It automatically calculates mathematical centering, spacing, Lucide icons, typography, native gradients, shadows, and optional 3D gloss bevels in a clean grouped object. Do NOT draw raw SVG curves or guess arbitrary text coordinates for UI elements. For individual shapes, add_shape and add_text support native "gradient" and "shadow".
VISUAL FEEDBACK: After generating visual designs or components, call get_preview to inspect the rendered result. If any alignment or styling needs fine-tuning, refine it with update_object.
PROJECTS: new_design/set_canvas, layer groups (list_layers...), export_design (PNG/JPG/SVG, or one object), export_project_file / import_project_file for .awandesign files. Saving files: ask the user first, then pass user_approved: true; files go only to the folder the user set in AWANDESIGN_EXPORT_DIR (.mcp.json). delete_project is permanent: ask the user first.
